hook: The $20 all-you-can-eat AI editor is gone, and its replacement is an $8 tier that only runs Grok and a $30 tier where Claude and GPT tokens bill on top. Both Cursor and GitHub Copilot are now agent-first and credit-metered, and each one restricts its entry tier in a different place.

sections.title: Your editor budget now buys a different contract
sections.content:
A renewal priced on the old $20 tier now buys either $8 Plus, which is Grok-only, or $30 Premium, where Claude and GPT tokens bill at API list price on top.

Two questions decide it: do you need non-Grok models, and does your review happen in GitHub PRs?

> Cursor told Reuters it runs at about $2.6B annualised revenue; SpaceX bought it in an all-stock deal at a $60B valuation.

Cursor's ownership changed before this renewal decision. Cursor is now a wholly owned SpaceX subsidiary.

- 21 April 2026: SpaceX and Cursor announced a partnership with a $10B payment and a $60B acquisition option.
- 16 June 2026: SpaceX signed the all-stock deal at a $60B valuation.
- 14 August 2026: the deal closed; Cursor joined the SpaceXAI team (SpaceX absorbed xAI in February 2026) to work on Grok, Grok Build, Grok Bot, Grok API and Cursor.

> Cursor states its constraint was compute: “We've wanted to push our training efforts much further, but we've been bottlenecked by compute.”

sections.title: Model ownership and repository ownership impose different limits
sections.content:
**Cursor's philosophy: the model is the product**, so the editor owns the model and the inference bill. Its own price sheet says so — Plus at $8 offers only Grok models, while Premium opens third-party access billed separately at API list price.

**GitHub sells the repository**, so Copilot's AI lands in PRs and reviews. That forbids giving review away: Free gets agent mode and the CLI, but PR review waits for the $10 Pro tier.

Cursor pushes back on that line — Premium lists code hosting via Origin and AI code review via Bugbot — but the two still compete on different surfaces: Cursor's $8 Plus cannot run Claude or GPT, and Copilot Free cannot review a PR.

sections.title: The meters punish different habits
sections.content:
Cursor's meter punishes third-party model use specifically: no plan includes those tokens, so Claude or GPT work passes through at API list price. Copilot's meter is a single credit pool per user that agent mode, review, cloud and CLI all drain.

| Vendor's monthly offer | Usage that incurs the penalty |
|---|---|
| Cursor: $8 Plus; $30 Premium | Plus is Grok-only; Premium adds third-party models at API list price on top |
| GitHub Copilot: $10 Pro ($15 credits); $39 Pro+ ($70 credits, Opus included); $100 Max ($200 credits) | Agent mode, review, cloud, CLI and app consume the same credit meter |

When a Copilot seat exhausts its credits, Pro and above buy extra.

| Buyer | Cursor | GitHub Copilot |
|---|---|---|
| 10 centrally managed organization seats | Teams 10 × $30+ = $300+/month base | Business 10 × $19 = $190/month base |
| Claude-dependent developer | Premium $30 plus metered tokens | Pro+ $39 with $70 of credits |
| Heavy user | Super $100 (15× Plus) | Max $100 ($200 credits) |

sections.title: Model neutrality now needs a renewal check
sections.content:
Teams that chose Cursor partly to stay model-agnostic now buy from a company whose model is Grok. Ownership changed the incentive. It does not prove that every request routes to Grok.

> Cursor states that Grok 4.6, the first joint model, scores between 69.9% and 70.8% on CursorBench and 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.

Before renewing, replay representative repository tasks and record the separately billed third-party usage.

- On Premium, compare the separate third-party token charge with the Claude or GPT work your team believes it ran; a low bill alone does not establish which model handled a request. Check model selections and available request/usage records before drawing routing conclusions.
- Do not buy Plus if non-Grok access is a requirement; test Premium's unbundled bill before committing.

sections.title: Copilot Free runs the agent; PR review costs $10
sections.content:
GitHub's counter-argument is reach: Copilot runs in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Xcode, Eclipse, Neovim, Zed and on github.com. Copilot Free already supports agent mode and the CLI, with limited usage.

- Copilot in the cloud starts at Pro.
- PR review, file diff review and custom instructions start at Pro.
- Assigning work to Copilot so it creates a pull request also starts at Pro.

A successful CLI trial does not establish that Free can perform your review workflow.

> Pro's $15 of monthly credits per user ($10 base + $5 flex) funds agent mode, code review and cloud work alike.

Try the actual handoff from assigned work to reviewed PR before migrating the team.

sections.title: Choose Grok commitment or repository consolidation today
sections.content:
Teams happy on Grok should buy Cursor; teams whose review lives in GitHub PRs should buy Copilot Pro. Cursor's $8 Plus undercuts Copilot Pro by $2, but only if Grok is enough.

- Choose Cursor if Grok meets your workload and third-party usage is optional.
- Choose GitHub Copilot if review and assigned PR work matter more than owning a separate editor workflow.

Moving to Copilot puts custom instructions (`.instructions.md`) and PR review behind Pro; moving to Cursor puts Claude and GPT behind list-price billing.

> If you need Claude inside a known monthly allotment, Copilot Pro+ at $39 includes Opus within $70 of credits; Cursor bills third-party tokens at API list price on top of $30 Premium.

Today, list the workflows that need Claude or GPT and price them on both plans.

decision_matrix.situation: Grok meets the workload and third-party access is unnecessary
decision_matrix.why: Plus's Grok-only restriction costs nothing when Grok is enough, and $8 undercuts Copilot Pro's $10.

decision_matrix.situation: Reviews and assigned PR work belong in the existing GitHub process
decision_matrix.why: Pro opens those repository-side workflows under the same credit meter.

decision_matrix.situation: A free trial must run inside JetBrains, Xcode or Neovim
decision_matrix.why: Copilot Free includes agent mode, and GitHub lists those editors among its supported surfaces.

decision_matrix.situation: Cheapest paid tier with AI PR review
decision_matrix.why: PR review starts at $10/user/month on Copilot; Cursor lists Bugbot code review on the $30 Premium tier.

decision_matrix.situation: Claude-class models must fit a known monthly allotment
decision_matrix.why: Pro+ includes premium models including Opus inside $70 of monthly credits for $39, while Cursor bills third-party tokens at API list price on top.

decision_matrix.situation: An existing Cursor team requires access to particular model providers
decision_matrix.pick: Verify model access, routing records and organizational controls
decision_matrix.why: Do not infer routing from a low bill. Compare Cursor Teams with Copilot Business for organization seats; personal plans are a separate buying decision.

decision_matrix.situation: One heavy agent user with a $100/month budget
decision_matrix.pick: Copilot Max if non-Grok models matter; Cursor Super if Grok suffices
decision_matrix.why: Max includes $200 of credits for $100; Super gives 15× Plus usage, and any third-party tokens still bill at API list price on top.

cost_math.label: 10 centrally managed organization seats, base subscriptions only
cost_math.result: Cursor starts at least $110/month higher before usage, taxes and extras. Individual Copilot Pro is not the organizational-seat equivalent.

cost_math.label: One Claude-dependent developer
cost_math.formula: Cursor Premium $30/month plus metered tokens at API list price vs Copilot Pro+ $39/month with $70 of included credits
cost_math.result: Copilot holds at $39 until the $70 of credits run out; Cursor's third-party cost has no published ceiling.

cost_math.label: Heavy user at $100/month
cost_math.formula: Cursor Super $100 (15× Plus usage) vs Copilot Max $100 ($200 of credits)
cost_math.result: Same price: Super buys 15× Plus volume with third-party tokens still billed on top; Max buys $200 of credits per user.

verdict_summary: For individuals, compare Cursor Plus/Premium with Copilot Pro/Pro+ using the models and usage you need. For centrally managed teams, compare Cursor Teams from $30+/user/month with Copilot Business at $19/user/month, then account for usage and controls. A personal Pro subscription is not an organizational-seat substitute.

faqs.q: Does Copilot require moving to a particular editor?
faqs.a: No. Beyond the major editors, GitHub lists Raycast, SQL Server Management Studio and GitHub Mobile among Copilot's supported surfaces.

faqs.q: What else does Cursor Premium bundle?
faqs.a: Premium gives 4× the usage of Plus, the latest Grok models, cloud agents and automations, and Grok Bot.

faqs.q: What do Cursor's higher individual tiers advertise?
faqs.a: Super is $100/month for 15× Plus usage and priority model access at peak times, the same price as Copilot Max with $200 of credits. Ultra is $200/month for 50× Plus usage and earliest access to all products and models.

faqs.q: What distinguishes Copilot Pro+ beyond its subscription price?
faqs.a: GitHub lists $70/month in total credits, premium models including Opus, and audit logs for Pro+.

tool_a.name: Cursor
tool_a.tagline: The editor that owns the model — now a SpaceX subsidiary
tool_a.realtime: Cloud agents and automations from Premium
tool_a.ai_readiness: Own models trained on SpaceX compute
tool_a.lock_in: High: Grok-first routing after the acquisition
pros: Owns its models, so it optimises the whole loop rather than renting someone's API
One editor, one bill for indexing, completion, agent and cloud automation
Premium bundles cloud agents, code hosting via Origin and review via Bugbot
$8 Plus is the cheapest agentic editor entry point if Grok is enough for you
cons: Every third-party model token bills at API list price on top of the subscription
Plus ($8) cannot run Claude or GPT at all
Model neutrality ended with the $60B acquisition; Grok is the default
Published benchmark numbers are the vendor's own (69.9–70.8% CursorBench)

tool_b.name: GitHub Copilot
tool_b.tagline: The repository vendor that puts AI where review happens
tool_b.realtime: Copilot in the cloud: assign work, get a PR (Pro+)
tool_b.ai_readiness: Premium models incl. Opus on Pro+
tool_b.lock_in: Medium: one credit pool inside GitHub
pros: Runs in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Xcode, Eclipse, Neovim, Zed and on github.com
Free already includes agent mode and the CLI — the entry tier is usable, not a demo
One credit meter covers agent, review, cloud and CLI, so spend is predictable per seat
Review lands where the team already reviews: PRs, file diffs, assigned work
cons: PR review, file diff review, custom instructions and cloud assignment all start at $10 Pro
Pro's $15 of credits is a budget, not an allowance you can ignore
Agent quality tracks whatever model GitHub routes you to; Opus is Pro+
You are buying into GitHub's surface — fine in GitHub, awkward outside it
